title: Search and read the Annals knowledge library
summary: Search the evidence-backed map of ideas, read supporting quotations or retained documents, and inspect source activity and revision history.
use_when: Concept labels, ancestor context, graph neighborhoods, exact supporting quotations, corpus revisions, or delivery metadata should be inspected.
A retained work's complete unchanged text should be retrieved by known label.
do_not_use_when: New material should be retained or reconciled.
Semantic similarity, web research, truth adjudication, or source-content topic search is expected.
The request concerns account usage rather than corpus knowledge.
outcome: A bounded local read from an explicitly resolved immutable corpus revision or from Annals delivery and work history, with the query's limits made visible.
effects: Reads the selected Annals library without invoking Nucleus, a model, or the network.
Search performs lexical matching over normalized concept labels and ancestor-label context only.
Graph responses are bounded and report a frontier when depth or node limits truncate the neighborhood.
authority: The Annals library is authoritative for retained works, concepts, parent edges, evidence links, reconciliations, commits, revisions, and delivery records.
An evidence link proves exact source support for a concept; it does not establish objective truth.
success: The response identifies the resolved revision, selected concept IDs or works, evidence, pagination, and any graph frontier required to interpret the result.
A lexical search is described as lexical and does not imply semantic recall.
Historical reads leave HEAD and all library state unchanged.
failure_and_recovery: Use public `cN` IDs rather than labels or paths to select existing concepts.
Opaque cursors are bound to the same library, command, query, scope, and revision; restart the read if that context changes.
Choose another `lately --by` basis when a delivery lacks the timestamp needed for the requested window.
privacy: Concept labels, exact quotations, retained source text, and delivery metadata are read from the local private library.
This capability sends no content to a model or network service.
does_not_authorize: Any corpus mutation or reconciliation application.
A truth claim beyond the exact retained evidence.
External disclosure of private library content.

consumers.statement: A local reader may inspect retained works, evidence-backed concepts, graph neighborhoods, source-delivery metadata, or corpus revision history.
This surface is not semantic similarity, source-content topic search, web research, truth adjudication, account reporting, or corpus mutation.

preconditions.statement: The caller selects a readable compatible Annals library and uses public concept IDs, work labels, revisions, filters, or opaque cursors accepted by the chosen command.

inputs.statement: Supported reads accept lexical query words, public cN concept IDs, work labels, revision selectors, bounded graph options, source-activity filters, or a context-bound opaque page cursor as applicable.
Labels and concept paths cannot select concepts, and source text, semantic vectors, objective-truth predicates, or arbitrary SQL are not search inputs.

outputs.statement: Outputs identify the resolved revision and return bounded concept, graph, evidence, work, delivery, commit, or revision-difference records with pagination and any truncation frontier visible.
Work show returns complete retained text; lately returns delivery metadata and never searches or emits source content or document-internal dates.

data_semantics.statement: Lexical search matches normalized concept labels and derived ancestor-label context; it is not semantic similarity, evidence retrieval, or a truth claim.
Evidence is an exact retained quotation supporting a concept across its parent relationships, not proof of objective truth or evidence attached to one edge.
A graph frontier marks where configured depth or node limits stopped expansion and is not necessarily a leaf or the complete graph.

identity_and_units.statement: Durable lowercase cN IDs select concepts, normalized-unique labels select works, and integer revisions select immutable corpus states; concept labels and paths are not identities.
Graph depth is measured in explicit parent-edge hops, maximum nodes and page limits are record counts, and lately windows use the selected delivery timestamp basis.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A command resolves HEAD once by default or reads one selected immutable historical revision; its output reports pagination and any graph frontier needed to qualify completeness.
Work show returns the complete selected retained source, while paged results are complete only for the reported page and fixed cursor context.
No wall-clock read latency, unlimited graph expansion, or indefinite cursor validity across changed command context is promised.

access.statement: The supported boundary is a local read through the Annals CLI against an explicitly resolved private library.
No model, network, mutation, direct SQLite, or external disclosure surface is provided by exploration.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Reads leave HEAD and library state unchanged, and historical corpus states are reconstructed from canonical commit effects.
Opaque cursors remain bound to the same library, command, query, scope, and revision; a changed context requires restarting pagination.
Commit history records applied corpus transitions, not work retention, no-change interpretations, model runs, or failed deliveries.

operational_limits.statement: Graph expansion is bounded by direction, depth, and maximum nodes; search is lexical; lately can omit a delivery lacking the selected timestamp basis.
No universal maximum corpus size, result throughput, query latency, or cursor-retention interval is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 1 is distinct from provider release and library schema; opaque cursors are not a parseable compatibility interface.
No cross-release cursor compatibility, output-schema support window, or deprecation period is promised.

reliances.statement: Exploration reads only the selected Annals library and invokes no Nucleus, model, network, or other product.
